name: common-qa-mcp

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Validate the configured connection and return provider, org/project and entity counts.

tools.name: qa_connect
tools.description:
Point this MCP at your QA product so it can work with EXISTING test cases -- list them, read their steps, modify them, and run them. Ask the user for their app URL and a token; do not guess either. The token is a product session JWT (then `projectId` is required, because the token alone carries no project context) or an MCP API key (then pass auth:"key" and projectId is optional -- a key is already project-scoped).

The connection is VALIDATED before it is accepted (it fetches the project), so a wrong URL, token or project fails here with the reason rather than surfacing later as a confusing error, and a failed attempt leaves any working connection untouched. It is kept in memory for as long as the agent runs and is never written to disk or logged.

NOT needed to record a new test case: recording, the live editor and drafts work offline with nothing configured.

url.description: MCP endpoint to hop to — the product agent /mcp, used for recording and save-with-editor. OPTIONAL for a DIRECT (backend-REST) connection: pass `baseUrl` instead. Required when connecting through a remote product MCP. Must start with http:// or https://.

token.description: Bearer token: a product session JWT, or an MCP API key.

projectId.description: Project id. REQUIRED with a JWT; optional with an API key.

auth.description: Token kind. Omit to AUTO-DETECT from the token (JWT-shaped → "jwt"). "jwt" sends Authorization + x-project-id; "key" sends Authorization only.

product.description: Which product to route this connection to (the product selector; defaults to the primary product). For a remote product, also pass its agent MCP `/mcp` endpoint as `url`.

baseUrl.description: The product BACKEND REST base (QA_BASE_URL) for DIRECT data ops (list/read/save/run). Provide this for a direct connection; `url` is only needed for recording / save-with-editor.

tools.name: qa_switch_project
tools.description: Switch to a different project on the SAME connection — reuses the current URL + token, so you do NOT re-enter them. Pass the project id; if the user names a project, call list_projects first to resolve the name to an id. Validated before it is adopted, so a bad id leaves the current project in place.

projectId.description: The project id to switch to. Use list_projects to find it by name.

tools.name: qa_connection_status
tools.description: Report whether this MCP is connected to a QA product, which URL and project, how the credentials arrived (startup config vs qa_connect), and whether a token is present. The token value itself is never returned.

tools.name: qa_disconnect
tools.description: Forget the runtime URL and token and fall back to whatever the agent started with (usually nothing). Use it before connecting to a different app or project, or to stop this MCP reaching a backend at all. Offline authoring is unaffected.

tools.name: actions_catalog
tools.description: Static per-platform action-type vocabulary (web/android/api/database/mainframe), used for offline draft validation. No network call.

tools.name: tc_draft_from_tc
tools.description:
Fetch a REAL test case from the connected product and hydrate it into a draft, carrying the original tcId. Because the draft carries the id, a later `tc_save({ draftId })` UPDATES that SAME test case (preserving id, run history, parameters, testdata bindings, and suite membership) instead of creating a sibling.

Use this to apply a `story_sync_testcases` drift report:
  1. tc_draft_from_tc({ tcId })
  2. tc_draft_update({ draftId, ops: <filtered proposedOps> })
  3. tc_save({ draftId })
Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

tcId.description: The existing test-case id to load as a draft.

tools.name: tc_draft_create
tools.description:
MANUAL-ONLY authoring. Call this when the user asked for a MANUAL test case: they said "manual", "draft only", "plain prose", "no automation", or asked to cover a user story's acceptance criteria as manual cases. For those, this IS the right tool — call it.

Do NOT use for automated tests. "create a test case", "record this flow", "add a test for X" (with no "manual" qualifier) mean AUTOMATED — route to the `web` / `mainframe` sub-agent to RECORD with real locators instead.

Create a new in-memory test-case draft from steps you author yourself. Nothing is persisted -- no disk, no backend, no network. Use tc_draft_open to hand it to the test-case editor for viewing.

DO NOT USE THIS FOR A REAL WEB APPLICATION. Steps written here have no locators, so the test case cannot execute -- it only reads plausibly. Whenever there is an app you can reach (the user gives a URL, names an environment, or asks for a test of a real flow), call the `web` sub-agent instead: that captures real locators, real element names and real parameters, and is the DEFAULT way to create a web test case. You do not need the user to say "record" -- if a test case for a real app is wanted, recording is how it is made.

Legitimate uses: a MANUAL test case the user explicitly asked for (no automation), API/database steps that need no element binding, restructuring or drafting steps the user supplied verbatim, or sketching a plan when no app is reachable -- and say plainly that the result is not executable until recorded.

PARAMETERISE EVERY DYNAMIC VALUE — this is mandatory for manual test cases whenever the step names a URL, credential, product name, form value, expected string, or anything the tester will type / compare. Instead of hard-coding "Enter admin in the Username field", write "Enter ${username} in the Username field" and pass `data: { username: "admin" }` at the TC level. Every `${name}` token becomes a Local parameter in the product and the value from `data` populates the test case's default test-data row (ITR-1) automatically. Steps with no `${...}` tokens create no parameters — that is only correct for pure checklist verifications ("verify heading is visible"). If a step references a real value, tokenise it.

storyRef.description: Link this test case to a USER STORY — its id or business key (US_123, from story_list / story_get). Used when drafting MANUAL test cases for a story so they save linked to it.

folderOrModule.description: SimplifyQA-only: id of the MODULE / folder to file this test case under on save (from list_modules). ASK the user which module before drafting; SimplifyQA files test cases in a module tree. Walnut ignores this.

data.description: Default values for the `${name}` tokens in step descriptions — one entry per token. Populates the auto-created default test-data row (ITR-1) on save. Example: `{ username: "admin", password: "admin123", url: "https://saucedemo.com" }`.

tools.name: tc_draft_update
tools.description:
Apply one or more ops (set_meta | add_step | update_step | remove_step | move_step) to a draft. Steps renumber contiguously from 1 after every op.

STEP TYPE — for add_step / update_step on a MANUAL test case (tc.category === "manual", or every existing step arrived with stepType "manual"), pass `stepType: "manual"`. For an AUTOMATED test case pick the execution technology ("web", "api", "android", …). Getting this wrong routes the row to the wrong UI card and it renders blank in the desktop viewer.

tools.name: tc_draft_get
tools.description: Fetch a draft by id: readable steps table, validation summary, and the neutral TestCase.

tools.name: tc_draft_discard
tools.description: Delete an in-memory draft. Nothing was ever persisted, so there is nothing else to undo.

tools.name: tc_draft_open
tools.description: Show this draft in the product's real editor. Prefers the local agent's own native window when the agent is running; otherwise returns a link to open. The draft rides in the URL fragment -- nothing is uploaded, no backend call is made.

tools.name: tc_save
tools.description:
Validate a draft, then PERSIST it to the connected product — creating a NEW test case, or UPDATING the one it was opened from (when the draft carries an id). Returns the product id + a deep link. Requires a live connection (qa_connect); the persist is forwarded to the product MCP.
⚠️ CALL ONLY ON AN EXPLICIT USER SAVE INSTRUCTION (e.g. "save it", "save this", "persist it"). RECORDING or AUTHORING a test case is NOT a save instruction; neither is the user approving the content ("looks good", "nice"). After a recording/draft finishes, SHOW the steps and ASK — do NOT auto-save. When unsure whether a reply meant save, ASK rather than saving.

draftId.description: The draft id from tc_draft_create / tc_draft_open.

tools.name: tc_automate
tools.description: Read an EXISTING MANUAL test case and return a recording guide the model uses to drive a live recording via the connected agent's granular tools (web_launch_application, web_snapshot, web_click, web_enter_text, …, core_close_session). The Electron recorder window opens automatically on web_launch_application; each captured step streams into it. The user reviews and clicks Save in the recorder — that CREATES A NEW automated test case (via POST /tm/testcase); the source manual TC is left untouched. Pass `url` unless the manual steps already contain one, and `extra` for credentials / data / what to assert. Read-only from MCP: this tool composes text, it never writes. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: The manual test case id (or business key TC_123) to automate.

url.description: Starting URL for the recording (the app under test).

extra.description: Extra guidance for the recording: credentials, data, assertions.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects visible to the current connection — id, name and counts. Use this to resolve a project NAME to its id (e.g. before qa_switch_project when the user names a project). Requires a live connection.

tools.name: tc_list
tools.description: List or search EXISTING TEST CASES (TC_* ids) in the connected product. NOT for reusable functions: if the user asks for functions, FN_*, the function library, or reusable steps, use `list_functions` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "test case", "TC", "TC_", "scenario", "script". Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Returns a summary list — id, title, technology, execution type, status, step count. Use `tc_get` to read one in full. Read-only, product-neutral.

createdBy.description: Numeric userId of the creator. Pass "me" to filter by the current caller (needs QA_MCP_USER_ID for API-key auth). Resolve names to ids via list_users first.

updatedBy.description: Numeric userId of the last updater. Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

storyId.description: Only test cases tagged to this user story (id or business key, e.g. US_123).

moduleId.description: Only test cases filed under this module (id or business key, e.g. MO_12). SimplifyQA only — ignored elsewhere.

obsolete.description: True → only obsolete TCs; false → only non-obsolete. Omit to include both. The response summary always reports how many of the returned rows are obsolete.

filters.description: Extra raw column filters for project-configured columns with no dedicated parameter above (Release/Priority/custom fields) — use the field's backend key as `column`.

column.description: Backend field name to filter on, e.g. "priority", "moduleId", "customFields.Team".

value.description: Exact-match value (or substring when `regEx` is true).

regEx.description: Substring/regex match instead of exact equality.

tools.name: tc_get
tools.description:
Read a single EXISTING test case in full — metadata plus its steps as a readable table — from the connected product. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). `id` accepts the product's id or business key. Product-neutral: same shape on any connected product.

VERSIONS: SimplifyQA TCs can have multiple versions, each with its own steps. When the TC has more than one version and `versionId` is omitted, this tool REFUSES and lists the available versions — ASK the user which one to read, then call again with `versionId`. Pass `versionId: ''` (empty string) to accept the TC's currently-selected version. Single- version TCs are read directly. Providers without versioning (Walnut) ignore `versionId`.

id.description: The test case id (or business key) to read.

versionId.description: Version to read (an id from the TC's `versions[]`). Omit to trigger the ASK-user prompt when the TC has multiple versions. Pass '' (empty string) to accept the TC's currently-selected version without prompting.

tools.name: tc_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an existing test case in the connected product. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: call once with just `tcId` to preview the target (title + step count) and get a warning; then call again with `{ tcId, confirm: true }` to actually delete. Refuses to delete without `confirm:true`. `tcId` accepts the product's id or business key. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Product-neutral.

tcId.description: The test case id (or business key) to delete.

confirm.description: Set to true on the SECOND call to actually delete.

tools.name: tc_clone
tools.description:
FOR TEST CASES ONLY. NOT for reusable functions: if the user names an `FN_*` key or asks to clone a function, use `fn_clone` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "test case", "TC", "TC_", "scenario", "script".

Save an existing test case as a NEW copy in the SAME project + module — all steps, versions, test data (all environments), parameters, object refs, and nested function calls are carried over. Uses SimplifyQA's native TC/FN copy endpoint. `tcId` accepts the product's id or business key (`TC_*`).

Naming: pass `newName` for a custom title; otherwise the backend auto-names the copy as `{sourceName}_copy1`, `_copy2`, etc.

VERSIONS — TWO-STEP: call once WITHOUT `versions` to get a preview of the source's versions and confirm with the user which to clone; then call again with `versions` set. `versions:["*"]` clones every version; `versions:["v1.0","v2.0",...]` clones only those. The tool REFUSES to clone until `versions` is passed — the preview step is not skippable.

PERMISSION: requires the `copy_testcase_across_project` privilege on the project (admins have it by default; other roles need it granted). If you get a permission error, ask your project admin. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: The source test case id or business key (e.g. TC_123).

newName.description: Custom title for the copy. Omit to let the backend auto-name it (`{sourceName}_copy1`).

versions.description: REQUIRED to actually clone. Version NAMES to clone (e.g. ["v1.0"]), or ["*"] to clone every version. Omit on the first call to get a preview + version list; ask the user which they want; then call again with the chosen value.

tools.name: tc_save_as_new_version
tools.description:
FOR TEST CASES ONLY. NOT for reusable functions: if the user names an `FN_*` key or asks to snapshot / create a new version of a function, use `fn_save_as_new_version` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "test case", "TC", "TC_", "scenario", "script".

Freeze the CURRENT server state of a test case under a NEW version name — same TC id, a new version row with cloned steps. Mirrors the SimplifyQA UI "Save as new version" dialog (operation: SAVENEWVERSION). `tcId` accepts the numeric id or business key (`TC_*`).

`versionName` must be unique for this TC — the backend rejects duplicates.

`tdCopy` (default TRUE) clones the source version's testdata iterations across every environment. Pass `false` to copy only the iteration STRUCTURE — values are empty, and parameters without a project-level defaultValue get suffixed column names. That matches the FE's "Cancel" button on the testdata-copy prompt.

`sourceVersionId` picks which version to snapshot; omit to snapshot the TC's currently selected version. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: The test case id or business key (e.g. TC_123).

versionName.description: Name for the new version (must be unique for this TC).

tdCopy.description: Clone testdata iterations from the source version. Default: true.

sourceVersionId.description: Version to snapshot; defaults to the TC's current version.

tools.name: tc_steps_to_function
tools.description:
Take a subset of the steps on an EXISTING test case and save them as a new reusable function (SimplifyQA STEPSTOFN operation). Mirrors the FE "Save as function" modal. Steps are picked by their current `seq`, resequenced 1..N in the new function, and filed under `moduleId`. `tcId` accepts the numeric id or business key (TC_123). Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

CALL THIS when the user says things like "save these steps as a function", "convert the first N steps to a function", "extract these steps into a function". Show the steps of the TC first (via tc_get) so the user can confirm which `seq`s to extract, and ASK the user which module to file the new function under — call `list_modules` if the module id is not known.

`executionType` forces every picked step into the AUTOMATION or MANUAL bucket; omit to split by each step's own executionType (function will be DUO if both are present).

TESTDATA: iterations from the source TC version are copied to the new function by default. The backend prunes them to only the parameters the extracted steps reference (via key-based matching in tcfn.service.js `compareDatas` `isStepsToFn` mode), across every environment the source version has. Pass `copyTestData: false` if you explicitly want a bare function.

REPLACE-IN-SOURCE: pass `replaceInSource: true` to also splice a FUNCTION + FUNCTION_END pair back into the source TC in place of the extracted steps (mirrors the FE "Save & Replace" button). The extracted rows are soft-deleted; the backend automatically drops any testdata columns those steps owned and injects an FN cell (with the FN's per-env default iteration) into every TC iteration row. Requires a contiguous `stepSeqs` range and refuses picks that cross control-flow (IF/WHILE/FOR/DO) or nested FUNCTION brackets, and DUO/SYNCON TCs — those are v2 cases.

FAILURE MODE with replaceInSource: if the FN is created but the follow-up PUT fails, the error surfaces the new fn id + version id so you can retry or delete the phantom function.

tcId.description: The source test case id or business key (e.g. TC_123).

stepSeqs.description: Current `seq` numbers of the steps to extract (e.g. [1,2,3,4] for the first four). Must be contiguous when replaceInSource is true.

moduleId.description: Module id to file the new function under. Resolve via list_modules if unknown.

executionType.description: Force all picked steps into this bucket; omit to split by each step's own executionType.

copyTestData.description: Copy the source version's testdata iterations to the new function (backend prunes to only the params the extracted steps use). Default: true.

replaceInSource.description: Replace the extracted steps on the source TC with a FUNCTION + FUNCTION_END call to the new function. Default: false (create-only). Requires contiguous stepSeqs and refuses DUO/SYNCON/control-flow spans.

tools.name: story_list
tools.description: Pull up USER STORIES in the connected project — id, key (US_…), title, status. Give `search` to find stories by keyword (matches key / title / description / acceptance criteria). Use story_get to read one with its acceptance criteria, then draft manual test cases for it. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only and product-neutral.

search.description: Keyword to find stories (key / title / description / AC).

sprintId.description: Only stories that belong to this sprint (from list_sprints).

releaseId.description: Only stories that belong to this release (from list_releases).

createdBy.description: Numeric userId of the creator. Pass "me" to filter by the current caller (needs QA_MCP_USER_ID for API-key auth). Resolve names to ids via list_users first.

updatedBy.description: Numeric userId of the last updater. Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

ownerId.description: Numeric userId of the story OWNER (assignee). Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

filters.description: Extra raw column filters for project-configured columns with no dedicated parameter above (Feature/Epic/Priority/custom fields) — use the field's backend key as `column`.

column.description: Backend field name to filter on, e.g. "priority", "moduleId", "customFields.Team".

value.description: Exact-match value (or substring when `regEx` is true).

regEx.description: Substring/regex match instead of exact equality.

tools.name: story_get
tools.description: Read a single user story — title, description, and ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — from the connected product. `id` accepts the story id or its business key (US_123). Read this before drafting manual test cases so they cover the acceptance criteria. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: List RELEASES in SimplifyQA — id, name, state, planned dates. `scope` is required: "project" = releases attached to the currently connected project, "all" = every release the token can see. ASK the user which scope before calling — do not guess. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only.

scope.description: ASK the user first: "project" = current project only, "all" = every release visible to the token.

tools.name: list_sprints
tools.description: List SPRINTS in SimplifyQA — id, name, parent release, state, planned dates. Pass `releaseId` (from list_releases) to see sprints of one release; omit to see every sprint the token can see. To answer "how many stories in this sprint", follow up with story_list({ sprintId }). Requires a live connection. Read-only.

releaseId.description: Only sprints belonging to this release (from list_releases).

tools.name: list_functions
tools.description: List reusable FUNCTIONS in the connected project — the FN_* library of building blocks that test cases call as nested steps. NOT test cases: if the user asks for test cases, TCs, scenarios, or scripts, use `tc_list` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "functions", "reusable functions", "function library", "FN_", "shared steps", "building blocks". Returns id, key (FN_*), name, description, technology (WEB/API/ANDROID/IOS), execution type (MANUAL/AUTOMATION), review status, step count. Use `get_function` to read one in full (with its steps) and `delete_function` to soft-delete. SimplifyQA-only. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only.

search.description: Free-text search over the function name.

fnType.description: Filter by technology (WEB / API / ANDROID / IOS).

moduleId.description: Only functions filed under this module (id or business key, e.g. MO_12).

createdBy.description: Numeric userId of the creator. Pass "me" to filter by the current caller (needs QA_MCP_USER_ID for API-key auth). Resolve names to ids via list_users first.

updatedBy.description: Numeric userId of the last updater. Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

tools.name: get_function
tools.description: Read a single reusable FUNCTION in full — metadata, description, and steps as a readable table — from the connected product. `id` accepts the function's numeric id or its business key (e.g. FN_123). NOT for test cases: if the user asks to read / explain a TC or TC_* id, use `tc_get` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "function", "FN_", "reusable function", "explain this function". Use this to explain what a function does before calling it from a test case or before deleting it. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

id.description: The function id (or business key like FN_123) to read.

tools.name: delete_function
tools.description: Soft-delete a reusable FUNCTION in the connected product. NOT for test cases: if the user asks to delete a TC or TC_* id, use `tc_delete` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "function", "FN_", "reusable function". TWO-STEP CONFIRM: call once with just `id` to preview the target (name + step count) and get a warning; then call again with `{ id, confirm: true }` to actually delete. Refuses to delete without `confirm:true`. `id` accepts the function's numeric id or business key. The backend refuses to delete a function that is still referenced by a test case, another function, or a workflow — this tool surfaces those references so the user can remove them first.

id.description: The function id (or business key like FN_123) to delete.

confirm.description: Set to true on the SECOND call to actually delete.

tools.name: fn_clone
tools.description:
FOR REUSABLE FUNCTIONS ONLY. NOT for test cases: if the user names a `TC_*` key or asks to clone a test case / scenario / script, use `tc_clone` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "function", "reusable function", "FN_", "FN-".

Save an existing reusable FUNCTION as a NEW copy in the SAME project + module — all steps, versions, test data (all environments), parameters, object refs, and nested function calls are carried over. Uses SimplifyQA's native TC/FN copy endpoint with `type:'FN'`. `fnId` accepts the product's id or business key (`FN_*`).

Naming: pass `newName` for a custom title; otherwise the backend auto-names the copy as `{sourceName}_copy1`, `_copy2`, etc.

VERSIONS — TWO-STEP: call once WITHOUT `versions` to get a preview of the source's versions and confirm with the user which to clone; then call again with `versions` set. `versions:["*"]` clones every version; `versions:["v1.0","v2.0",...]` clones only those. The tool REFUSES to clone until `versions` is passed — the preview step is not skippable.

PERMISSION: requires the `copy_function_across_projects` privilege on the project (admins have it by default; other roles need it granted). If you get a permission error, ask your project admin. Requires a live connection.

fnId.description: The source function id or business key (e.g. FN_123).

newName.description: Custom title for the copy. Omit to let the backend auto-name it (`{sourceName}_copy1`).

versions.description: REQUIRED to actually clone. Version NAMES to clone (e.g. ["v1.0"]), or ["*"] to clone every version. Omit on the first call to get a preview + version list; ask the user which they want; then call again with the chosen value.

tools.name: fn_save_as_new_version
tools.description:
FOR REUSABLE FUNCTIONS ONLY. NOT for test cases: if the user names a `TC_*` key or asks to snapshot / create a new version of a test case, use `tc_save_as_new_version` instead. Trigger words for THIS tool: "function", "reusable function", "FN_", "FN-".

Freeze the CURRENT server state of a reusable FUNCTION under a NEW version name — same FN id, a new version row with cloned steps. Mirrors the SimplifyQA UI "Save as new version" dialog (operation: SAVENEWVERSION, type: FN). `fnId` accepts the numeric id or business key (`FN_*`).

`versionName` must be unique for this FN — the backend rejects duplicates.

`tdCopy` (default TRUE) clones the source version's testdata iterations across every environment. Pass `false` to copy only the iteration STRUCTURE — values are empty. That matches the FE's "Cancel" button on the testdata-copy prompt.

`sourceVersionId` picks which version to snapshot; omit to snapshot the FN's newest version (the FN doc has no inline current-version marker). Requires a live connection.

fnId.description: The function id or business key (e.g. FN_123).

versionName.description: Name for the new version (must be unique for this FN).

tdCopy.description: Clone testdata iterations from the source version. Default: true.

sourceVersionId.description: Version to snapshot; defaults to the FN's newest version.

tools.name: list_modules
tools.description: List the MODULES (folder tree) in the connected project — id, name, parent. Use for any "list / show / what modules" request. Also the source of the `folderOrModule` id passed to tc_draft_create (ask the user which one before drafting). SimplifyQA-only: Walnut has no module tree. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: get_module
tools.description: Fetch full detail for one MODULE — id, name, code, description, parentId, childIds. Use when list_modules' summary row isn't enough (need description or child tree). SimplifyQA-only. Requires a live connection.

id.description: Module id (numeric or business key resolvable via list_modules).

tools.name: create_module
tools.description: Create a new MODULE under the connected project. Set `isRoot:true` for a top-level folder; otherwise pass `parentId` (resolve via list_modules). Duplicate name in the same project is rejected server-side. SimplifyQA-only. Requires a live connection.

name.description: Module name. Must be unique within the project.

isRoot.description: True → top-level folder; false → child of `parentId`.

parentId.description: Parent module id (required when isRoot is false).

tools.name: delete_module
tools.description: Delete one or more MODULES by id. Two phases: call with `confirm:false` (default) for a DRY RUN that returns each id's dependency footprint (test cases, functions, parameters, objects, defects, user stories that still reference the module). Call again with `confirm:true` to actually delete; the server drops only ids with EMPTY dependencies and silently skips the rest — surface those to the caller so they can move/remove the refs first. SimplifyQA-only. Requires a live connection.

projectId.description: Project id the modules belong to.

tools.name: delete_version
tools.description: Soft-delete ONE version of a test case (`kind:"tc"`) or a reusable function (`kind:"fn"`) in the connected product. `versionId` comes from the parent's `versions[]` (populated by `tc_get` for TCs and `get_function` for FNs); pass the version's `name` too (backend validator requires it). TWO-STEP CONFIRM: call once with `confirm:false` (default) to get a DRY RUN — the response lists every entity still referencing this version (defects, suites, exec plans, scenarios, schedulers, pipelines, workflows for a TC; TCs, other FNs, workflows for a FN). Only when EVERY dependency map is empty is the delete allowed; the server itself REFUSES a `confirm:true` call when refs still exist, so `confirm:true` doesn't guarantee deletion — the tool inspects the response and reports honestly. Refuses to delete the LAST remaining version (the parent would be orphaned; use `tc_delete` / `delete_function` instead to remove the whole entity). SimplifyQA-only. Requires a live connection.

kind.description: 'tc' for a test-case version; 'fn' for a function version.

parentId.description: Parent TC or FN id (numeric or business key like TC_123 / FN_45).

versionId.description: The version's uuid (from tc_get.versions[].id or get_function.versions[].id).

versionName.description: The version's human name (e.g. 'v1.0'). Required by the backend validator.

confirm.description: False (default) → dry-run; true → apply delete (server still refuses if any dependency exists).

tools.name: suite_list
tools.description: List the test suites in the connected product — id, name, type (Manual/Automation, where the provider has a suite-level type — SimplifyQA does, Walnut doesn't), and member (test-case) count. Use suite_get to read one with its ordered members, or suite_run to execute one. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only and product-neutral.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List users the caller can see in the connected product — id, name, email, username, status. Use this to resolve a person's NAME to a userId before filtering tc_list / story_list by `createdBy` / `updatedBy`. Non-admin callers are auto-scoped server-side to users in their assigned projects. Optional `search` matches on name (case-insensitive substring). Optional `projectId` narrows further to that project's members. Requires a live connection. Read-only.

projectId.description: Only users assigned to this project (from list_projects).

tools.name: suite_get
tools.description: Read a single test suite — its name, description, and ORDERED member test cases — from the connected product. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). `id` is the suite id. Product-neutral: same shape on any connected product.

tools.name: suite_add_testcases
tools.description: Add one or more EXISTING test cases to a suite (appended in order). `tcIds` accepts ids or business keys (e.g. TC_123) — use suite_list / tc_list to find them. NOTE: a suite can only hold test cases of ONE category (all manual OR all automated) — the product rejects a mix. Requires a live connection. Returns the updated suite with its members.

suiteId.description: The suite id to add to (from suite_list).

tcIds.description: Test case ids / business keys to add.

tools.name: suite_remove_testcases
tools.description: Remove one or more test cases from a suite. `tcIds` accepts ids or business keys; every occurrence of each is removed and the remaining members are reordered. Requires a live connection. Returns the updated suite with its members.

suiteId.description: The suite id to remove from.

tcIds.description: Test case ids / business keys to remove.

tools.name: journal_grep
tools.description: Load a test case as NUMBERED steps to edit — from its recording JOURNAL when one exists (so a later journal_modify stays healer/re-record consistent), else from its persisted steps (the `source` is reported). Optional `pattern` filters shown rows (case-insensitive substring over the step description) to help locate a range for journal_modify. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: Test case id or business key.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive substring filter over step descriptions.

tools.name: journal_modify
tools.description:
Apply granular edits to an EXISTING test case and persist them, opening the result in the test-case editor. Use journal_grep first to see the numbered steps, then pass ops (numbers are from that view, 1-based):
  • add_step / update_step / remove_step / move_step — edit individual steps
  • wrap_in_loop { from, to, condition?, maxIterations? } — wrap steps from..to in a while loop
  • wrap_in_if   { from, to, condition? } — wrap steps from..to in an if block
  • insert_nested { at?, tcId, name? } — insert an existing test case as a nested step (reuse)
For a test case backed by a recording journal the journal is kept in sync (so healer / re-record stay consistent); others edit the persisted steps. NOTE: adding a brand-new INTERACTION step (click/type on a new element) via add_step has no captured locator, so it is a manual/non-executable step — capture new interactions by recording instead. Requires a live connection.

tcId.description: Test case id or business key.

tools.name: object_create
tools.description: Create a new object (a locator-bound UI element) in the shared Object Repository. `objectType` (e.g. "WEB", "ANDROID") is REQUIRED and STRUCTURAL — it selects the object template and cannot be changed after creation (see object_update). `locators` is the set of captured selector strategies for this element. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

name.description: Display name for the object (the UI's "Name" column).

objectType.description: Object type / technology, e.g. "WEB", "ANDROID", "IOS", "DESKTOP". Required, and fixed once created.

locators.description: Captured locator strategies for this element.

tools.name: object_list
tools.description: List or search objects (recorded, locator-bound UI elements) in the connected product's shared Object Repository. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Returns a summary — id, name, object type and locator count — never full locator bags (use object_get for one in full). Omit `limit`/`offset` to fetch the ENTIRE project object list (paged internally, up to 2000); pass either one to control a single page yourself instead.

query.description: Free-text search over the object name / description.

pageName.description: Filter by captured page / screen name.

limit.description: Return exactly one page of this size, starting at `offset`, instead of fetching everything.

offset.description: Result offset for a single manual page (implies a one-page fetch; default page size 100 if `limit` is omitted).

tools.name: object_get
tools.description: Read a single object from the shared Object Repository — its name, type, and FULL locator bag (every captured strategy, e.g. playwright primary + xpath fallbacks). Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

tools.name: object_update
tools.description: Update an object in the shared Object Repository — rename it, and/or fix locator values directly (e.g. a stale `data-test` attribute). `locators` UPSERTS by strategy name: an entry matching an EXISTING locator name updates its value/unique in place, everything else on the object is untouched, and a name with no existing match is added as a NEW locator — you do not need to resupply the full locator set. The object's TYPE (technology) and TEMPLATE ID are NOT editable here — they are structural (they determine which attribute set is even valid) and stay whatever they already are; changing either means creating a new object, not updating this one. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

name.description: New display name for the object.

locators.description: Locators to upsert by name, e.g. [{ name: "data-test", value: "123456" }] to fix one attribute — every other locator on the object is left as-is.

tools.name: object_delete
tools.description: Delete an object from the shared Object Repository. DEPENDENCY-CHECKED first: if the object is still referenced by any test case, function, or workflow, the delete is REFUSED — it reports what still uses it instead of silently breaking those. Only a dependency-free object is actually deleted. Requires a live connection (qa_connect).

tools.name: story_sync_testcases
tools.description:
Compare a user STORY against every MANUAL test case linked to it (via storyRef) and return a structured drift report: what changed (ac_added / ac_reworded / ac_removed / step_stale) and the exact draft ops (add_step / update_step / remove_step) to apply.

HOW TO APPLY THE REPORT (mandatory path — do not deviate):
  For each entry in `results[]`:
    1. tc_draft_open({ tcId: <testCaseId> })   ← loads the EXISTING TC as a draft, SAME id
    2. tc_draft_update({ draftId, ops: <proposedOps> })
    3. tc_save({ draftId })                    ← persists back to the SAME TC id
DO NOT delete the test case and recreate it. DO NOT create a sibling/replacement TC. In-place edit preserves the TC id, run history, existing parameters, testdata bindings, and suite membership — all of which are lost on delete+recreate. Even when the drift is large (new AC, restructured flow), the correct action is still edit-in-place via the three steps above. If the user needs a NEW test case for scope the existing TC does not cover, that is a separate authoring task (tc_draft_create), NOT part of applying this drift report.

AUTOMATION test cases are reported in `skipped` (v1 scope: manual only — automation drift needs recording, which is user-driven). Pass `testCaseIds` to limit the scan; otherwise the tool walks listTestCases and filters by storyRef (bounded by `scanLimit`, default 200). Report-only: this tool writes nothing itself. Requires a live connection.

testCaseIds.description: Restrict comparison to these TC ids/keys. Recommended for large projects; otherwise the tool walks up to `scanLimit` TCs.

sensitivity.description: Match-strictness for AC↔step overlap. strict=more drift flagged, loose=less. Default normal.

scanLimit.description: Cap on how many TCs to fetch when `testCaseIds` is omitted. Default 200.

tools.name: epic_list
tools.description: Pull up EPICS in the connected project — id, key (EP_…), name, state. Top of the backlog hierarchy: epic → feature → story. Use `search` for keyword matches on name. Requires a live connection. Read-only.

state.description: Filter by state (must match the project state config).

createdBy.description: Numeric userId of the creator. Pass "me" to filter by the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

updatedBy.description: Numeric userId of the last updater. Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

ownerId.description: Numeric userId of the owner (assignee). Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

tools.name: epic_get
tools.description: Read a single EPIC — name, state, description, dates, effort — by id or business key (EP_123). Requires a live connection. Read-only.

tools.name: epic_create
tools.description: Create a new EPIC in the connected project. `projectIds` defaults to the current project when omitted. Backend requires `name`, `state`, `estimatedEffort`, `plannedStartDate`, `plannedEndDate` — state must match an existing state in the project config (use epic_list or epic_get on an existing epic to see valid values).

state.description: State — must match the project state config.

projectIds.description: Project ids the epic belongs to. Defaults to [currentProject].

ownerId.description: Numeric userId of the epic owner.

tools.name: epic_update
tools.description: PATCH an existing EPIC — pass only the fields to change plus `updateVersion` (optimistic concurrency, from the last epic_get). Accepts id or business key (EP_123). Cannot rename the epic to a duplicate of another epic in the same customer.

updateVersion.description: Optimistic-concurrency version from the last read.

tools.name: feature_list
tools.description: Pull up FEATURES in the connected project — id, key (FT_…), name, state, parent epic. Middle of the backlog hierarchy. Pass `epicId` to list features under a specific epic. Requires a live connection. Read-only.

epicId.description: Only features under this parent epic id.

createdBy.description: Numeric userId of the creator. Pass "me" to filter by the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

updatedBy.description: Numeric userId of the last updater. Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

ownerId.description: Numeric userId of the owner (assignee). Pass "me" for the current caller. Resolve names via list_users first.

tools.name: feature_get
tools.description: Read a single FEATURE by id or business key (FT_123). Requires a live connection. Read-only.

tools.name: feature_create
tools.description: Create a new FEATURE. `projectIds` defaults to the current project when omitted. Link to a parent epic via `epicId`. Backend requires `name`, `estimatedEffort`, `plannedStartDate`, `plannedEndDate`.

tools.name: feature_update
tools.description: PATCH an existing FEATURE — pass only the fields to change plus `updateVersion` (optimistic concurrency, from the last feature_get). Accepts id or business key (FT_123).

tools.name: story_create
tools.description: Create a new USER STORY under the connected project. `projectId` defaults to the current project. Link to parents via `epicId` / `featureId`. Backend requires `name`, `state`, `estimatedEffort`. Pass `acceptanceCriteria` as a newline-separated string — one AC per line (the SQA `userstory.acceptanceCriteria` column is a single string).

state.description: State — must match the project state config.

tools.name: story_update
tools.description: PATCH an existing USER STORY — pass only the fields to change plus `updateVersion` (optimistic concurrency, from the last story_get). Accepts id or business key (US_123). Pass `acceptanceCriteria` as a newline-separated string when replacing AC lines.

tools.name: cloud_runners
tools.description: List the cloud runner VMs registered to the connected project and which are online. Use this to show the user the cloud options, or to pick a specific runner id for tc_run. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: local_agents
tools.description: List the LOCAL agents registered to the connected customer and which are online. Use this to show the user their local run options, or to pick a specific agent id (its credential_id) to pass as `agentId` to a LOCAL tc_run / suite_run. Requires a live connection. NOTE on online status: agents whose `machineName` matches this MCP host are reported online (mirrors sqa-ui's own-machine override — the DB `active` flag is only refreshed at first registration + a stale cron, so it lags behind). Other agents' status still comes from the DB.

tools.name: tc_run
tools.description:
Execute ONE existing test case in the connected product. ASK the user for EVERY field the Execute dialog asks — never assume — and in ORDER: (1) `releaseId` (from list_releases; pass '' if the user skips), (2) `sprintId` (from list_sprints; pass '' if the user skips), (3) `versionId` (from tc_get's `versions[]`; pass '' to accept the TC's current version), (4) `environment` (from tc_list_environments — required), (5) `browser` (required), (6) `mode` local/cloud, (7) `when` immediate/schedule, (8) for a schedule the start time + recurrence + timezone, (9) THEN offer the eligible agent/runner and pass the pick. The tool REFUSES when any of (1)-(7) is omitted — that is deliberate; it forces the ask instead of silently defaulting. `mode` decides WHERE it runs:
  • 'local' — a local agent's own browser. Pass `agentId` from local_agents. For when:'immediate' only ONLINE agents are eligible (a run-now can't target an offline agent; omit to auto-pick your own online agent). For when:'schedule' ANY agent (online OR offline) is eligible and `agentId` is REQUIRED.
  • 'cloud' — an online cloud runner VM (ONLINE-only whether now or scheduled). Pass `cloudRunnerId` from cloud_runners; for a schedule omit it to let the backend auto-pick a live VM at fire time.
IF THE USER HAS NOT SAID local or cloud, ASK — this tool refuses when `mode` is omitted. For cloud, if no runner is online it reports that there are no active cloud runners (nothing is run).
`when` decides WHEN it runs (this tool REFUSES when `when` is omitted — ASK the user):
  • 'immediate' — dispatch now; returns the run id — poll run_status for the result.
  • 'schedule' — create a schedule instead (requires `scheduledFor`); ASK the start time, recurrence, end date and timezone BEFORE offering an agent. Returns the schedule id.
NOTE: MANUAL test cases cannot be run or scheduled by an agent — the backend rejects them.

tcId.description: The test case id (or business key) to run.

mode.description: Where to run. REQUIRED — ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted).

agentId.description: For local: a specific agent credential_id (from local_agents). when:'immediate' → must be an ONLINE agent (or omit to auto-pick your own online agent); when:'schedule' → REQUIRED, and may be an offline agent (it runs when it fires).

releaseId.description: Tag the run with a RELEASE (from list_releases). Optional in the UI; omit to leave untagged.

sprintId.description: Tag the run with a SPRINT (from list_sprints). Optional in the UI; omit to leave untagged.

versionId.description: Override the TC's currently-selected VERSION for this run (an id from the TC's `versions[]`). Omit to run the current version — that's what the UI's Version chip defaults to.

environment.description: Environment key (from tc_list_environments). ASK the user before running — the UI marks this required.

browser.description: Browser, default 'chromium' (bundled + isolated). Others: 'chrome'/'msedge' (installed channel), 'firefox', 'webkit'. NOTE: a schedule accepts only chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit.

headless.description: Headless. Defaults: cloud=true, local=false. (Immediate runs only.)

cloudRunnerId.description: For cloud: a specific ONLINE runner id (from cloud_runners). For when:'schedule' omit to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.

deviceId.description: REQUIRED for ANDROID/IOS test cases — the target device id. LOCAL: adb serial or emulator name. CLOUD: the marketplace device name. Enumerate with android_list_devices.

when.description: When to run — REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted). 'immediate' dispatches now; 'schedule' creates a schedule (needs scheduledFor).

scheduledFor.description: REQUIRED for when:'schedule' — ISO datetime of the first/only run (e.g. '2026-08-20T09:00:00Z').

scheduleType.description: Recurrence for a schedule. Default 'once'. hourly/daily/weekdays require an endDate.

endDate.description: For a recurring schedule — ISO end date (required for hourly/daily/weekdays).

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a schedule (e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'). Default 'UTC'.

tools.name: suite_run
tools.description:
Execute an existing test SUITE — all its member test cases, in order — in the connected product. ASK the user for EVERY field the UI's Execute-suite dialog asks — never assume — and in ORDER (mirrors the product UI, `_parentComponent==="SU"`): (1) `releaseId` (from list_releases — the UI marks it required with `*` for a suite), (2) `sprintId` (from list_sprints — also `*` for a suite), (3) `environment` (from tc_list_environments — `*`), (4) `mode` local/cloud, (5) `when` immediate/schedule, (6) for a schedule the start time + recurrence + timezone, (7) THEN offer the eligible agent/runner. The tool REFUSES when any of (1)–(5) is omitted — that is deliberate; it forces the ask instead of silently defaulting. UNLIKE `tc_run`, a suite does NOT ask for `versionId` or `browser` — each TC in the suite carries its own pinned version + execution platform (that's what the suite editor picks per row). `mode` decides WHERE it runs:
  • 'local' — a local agent's own browser, always serial. Pass `agentId` from local_agents. For when:'immediate' only ONLINE agents are eligible (omit to auto-pick your own online agent); for when:'schedule' ANY agent (online OR offline) is eligible and `agentId` is REQUIRED.
  • 'cloud' — online cloud runner VM(s) (ONLINE-only whether now or scheduled). Pass `cloudRunnerId` from cloud_runners; for a schedule omit it to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.
For cloud, if no runner is online it reports that there are no active cloud runners (nothing is run).
`when` decides WHEN it runs:
  • 'immediate' — dispatch now; returns the suite-run id — poll run_status for progress (per-test-case results under `children`) and run_stop to cancel.
  • 'schedule' — create a schedule instead (requires `scheduledFor`); ASK the start time, recurrence, end date and timezone BEFORE offering an agent. Returns the schedule id.
NOTE: a suite of only MANUAL test cases cannot be run or scheduled by an agent — the backend rejects it.

suiteId.description: The suite id to run (from suite_list / suite_get).

releaseId.description: REQUIRED for a suite (UI marks it `*` for _parentComponent==="SU"). A release id from list_releases. Ask the user.

sprintId.description: REQUIRED for a suite (UI marks it `*` for _parentComponent==="SU"). A sprint id from list_sprints (scoped to the picked release). Ask the user.

mode.description: Where to run. REQUIRED — ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted).

agentId.description: For local: a specific agent credential_id (from local_agents). when:'immediate' → must be ONLINE (or omit to auto-pick your own online agent); when:'schedule' → REQUIRED, may be offline.

environment.description: Environment key (from tc_list_environments). REQUIRED — the UI marks this with a red asterisk for a suite.

browser.description: Optional at the SUITE level — each TC in the suite has its own execution platform (that's the suite-editor pick per row). Provide only to OVERRIDE for every WEB TC. Values: 'chromium' (default), 'chrome'/'msedge', 'firefox', 'webkit'. NOTE: a schedule accepts only chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit.

headless.description: Headless. Defaults: cloud=true, local=false. (Immediate runs only.)

cloudRunnerId.description: For cloud: a specific ONLINE runner id (from cloud_runners). For when:'schedule' omit to auto-pick a live VM at fire time.

strategy.description: Cloud dispatch order across the suite (immediate runs). Default serial; local is always serial.

maxConcurrent.description: Cloud batch/dynamic only — max test cases running at once (immediate runs).

terminateOnFailure.description: Stop dispatching remaining test cases after the first failure (immediate runs).

when.description: When to run — REQUIRED, ASK the user if unstated (the tool refuses when omitted). 'immediate' dispatches now; 'schedule' creates a schedule (needs scheduledFor).

scheduledFor.description: REQUIRED for when:'schedule' — ISO datetime of the first/only run (e.g. '2026-08-20T09:00:00Z').

scheduleType.description: Recurrence for a schedule. Default 'once'. hourly/daily/weekdays require an endDate.

endDate.description: For a recurring schedule — ISO end date (required for hourly/daily/weekdays).

timezone.description: IANA timezone for a schedule (e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'). Default 'UTC'.

tools.name: run_status
tools.description: Read the status of a run started by tc_run — state (queued/running/passed/failed/stopped/error), step progress, and a link. Requires a live connection.

runId.description: The run id returned by tc_run.

tools.name: run_stop
tools.description: Signal a running execution to stop. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List the scheduled runs in the connected project — each with WHAT it runs (test case / suite), its cadence, next run time, status (scheduled / running / paused / cancelled), where it runs + the pinned agent, and its browser. Use this to find a schedule to edit, pause/resume, cancel, or delete. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Change a schedule's time / recurrence / end date / timezone / browser / environment, or RE-PIN its agent. Pass `scheduleId` (from schedule_list) and ONLY the fields to change. To re-pin: mode:'local' + `agentId` (from local_agents), or mode:'cloud' + a runner's `cloudRunnerCredentialId` (the `credentialId` from cloud_runners). Requires a live connection.

endDate.description: New ISO end date (for recurring schedules).

browser.description: New browser (schedules accept chromium/msedge/firefox/webkit, not chrome).

mode.description: Re-pin target: pair with agentId (local) or cloudRunnerCredentialId (cloud).

agentId.description: Local re-pin: an agent credential_id from local_agents.

cloudRunnerCredentialId.description: Cloud re-pin: a runner's credentialId from cloud_runners.

tools.name: schedule_control
tools.description: Change a schedule's state: `pause` (stop it firing but keep it — reversible with `resume`), `resume` (re-enable a paused schedule), or `cancel` (stop its pending / live run). To remove a schedule entirely, use schedule_delete instead. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Permanently DELETE a schedule (and tear down any run it currently owns). This cannot be undone — to only stop it temporarily use schedule_control (pause / cancel). CONFIRM with the user before deleting. Requires a live connection.

tools.name: tc_list_environments
tools.description: List every environment configured for the currently connected project (e.g. general, staging, production). Testdata is stored PER ENVIRONMENT — each env has its own iteration rows. ALWAYS call this before tc_get_testdata / tc_generate_testdata, show the user the options, and ASK which env they want to generate testdata for. Never assume. The value to pass onward as `environmentType` is the `key` field on each returned env.

tools.name: tc_get_testdata
tools.description: Fetch the default iteration (template row) for TC `tcId` in a specific environment — the parameter list plus the CURRENT seed values. Testdata is per-env: seeds may differ across envs. `environmentType` is REQUIRED — this tool refuses when it is omitted, since silently guessing an env previously caused false "testdata not found" results. FIRST call tc_list_environments and ask the user which env they want. Then read the template here, and use the seeds + the test case's steps (from tc_get) to reason about realistic values before calling tc_generate_testdata.

tcId.description: Test case id (or business key like TC_123).

environmentType.description: Env `key` (from tc_list_environments). REQUIRED — this tool refuses when omitted. Ask the user which env before reading testdata.

tools.name: tc_generate_testdata
tools.description:
Persist up to 20 testdata rows for TC `tcId` into a SPECIFIC environment. Testdata is stored per environment — rows saved here only affect the env you pass. WORKFLOW: (1) call tc_list_environments and ASK the user which env; (2) call tc_get_testdata with that env to read seeds; (3) call this tool with the SAME `environmentType`. `environmentType` is REQUIRED here — this tool refuses when it is omitted. Two ways to feed values:
  1) Model-generated — pass `rows: [{paramName: value}, ...]`. Call tc_get_testdata first for the parameter names + seeds, tc_get for step context, then produce rows that fit the flow.
  2) Formula-driven — pass `formulas: {paramName: {name, args?}}` (names from tc_list_formulas). The adapter evaluates each formula per row via /tm/customFormula and stamps both the value and the source `=NAME(...)` expression. Use `count` to say how many rows, or provide `rows` for constant columns; mixing is fine (formulas win over row values for the same param).
Rows are appended as new iterations; they do not become the default. Hard cap: 20 rows.

tcId.description: Test case id (or business key like TC_123).

rows.description: Rows keyed by param name (from tc_get_testdata). 1..20 rows. Omit when using formulas + count.

count.description: How many rows to generate when using formulas without explicit rows. Ignored if rows is set.

formulas.description: Per-column formula assignments applied to every row. Outer keys are param names from tc_get_testdata. Wins over rows[i] for the same key.

name.description: RAW formula name from tc_list_formulas — the identifier only, no parens, no arg list. Correct: "FIRST_NAME". Wrong: "FIRST_NAME()", "FIRST_NAME(country,sex)".

args.description: Named args. Keys MUST match Formula.parameters[].keyName exactly, no trailing colons or extra whitespace. Correct: {"country name": "United States"}. Wrong: {"country name:": "..."}.

environmentType.description: Env `key` (from tc_list_environments). REQUIRED — this tool refuses when omitted. Ask the user which env before generating.

tools.name: tc_list_formulas
tools.description: Return the formulas the connected project can use for testdata generation — DEFAULT prefabs (FIRST_NAME, RANDOM_EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, …) plus any CUSTOM formulas defined at customer or project scope. Each entry carries a signature (parameter list), an example, and the accepted argument keys. Feed a chosen `{name, args}` into `tc_generate_testdata.formulas` and that column will be auto-filled fresh per row via the product /tm/customFormula service. Use this when the user says "use a formula" / "generate email with our formula" / "list formulas".

tools.name: defect_list
tools.description: List defects (bugs) raised in the connected project — id/code, title, state, severity, priority, assignee(s), and which test case(s) each is linked to. Mirrors the filters on the product's Defect list page: `search` (title keyword), `tcId` (defects against one test case), `storyId` (defects on one user story), `state` (workflow state — use the exact `state` value from an existing defect_list row, e.g. "new"/"open"/"closed", not the capitalized UI label), `assignedTo` / `createdBy` (numeric userId, or "me" — resolve a name to an id via list_users first). The Defect list page also lets a user filter by MANY MORE project-configured columns (Module, Release, Feature, Team, Client, Labels, custom fields, ...) that vary per project — pass those via `filters: [{ column, value }]` (raw column filters, appended as-is; use the field's backend key, e.g. `moduleId`/`releaseId`/`featureId`/`teamId`/`clientId`/`tags`). Omit everything for the full project list. Requires a live connection (qa_connect). Read-only and product-neutral.

search.description: Keyword to find defects by title.

tcId.description: Only defects raised against this test case (id or business key).

storyId.description: Only defects linked to this user story (id or business key).

tools.name: tc_heal
tools.description:
Replays a failed test case live, captures the DOM at the failing step, classifies the failure (LOCATOR / TIMING / IFRAME / STALE / ASSERTION_TEXT / DATA / APP_BUG / ENV / FLAKY / UNKNOWN), and proposes a fix. Every response carries the classification and a human rationale — even when the failure is not healable (product bug, bad data, env).

  • mode='suggest' (default) — diagnose and propose, do not write.
  • mode='apply' — persist the fix as a NEW test-case version (never overwrites).
  • mode='apply_and_verify' — apply then re-run the test case; result in `verified`.

  • scope='tc' (default) — patch the step's own objectRef.locators (TC-local).
  • scope='object' — patch the shared object's attribute chain (heals every TC that uses it; opt-in, higher blast radius).

Locator fixes always APPEND a new strategy; the original locators are preserved as fallbacks so a bad proposal cannot destroy the recorded intent. Runs are capped at `maxAttemptsPerStep` retries per step (default 3).

runId.description: Specific failed run to heal against. Omit to use the latest failed run for tcId.

mode.description: Default 'suggest'. 'apply' persists a new version; 'apply_and_verify' also re-runs the TC.

scope.description: Default 'tc'. 'object' patches the shared object library — heals every TC using it.

url.description: Override start URL for the replay session (if the TC lacks a navigate step).

maxAttemptsPerStep.description: Cap on heal retries at the failing step. Default 3.

dryRun.description: Classify + propose from existing objectRef.locators only. No browser session opened.
